title: Social Security Numbers: Less Boring Than You'd Think
summary: Josh and Chuck explain Social Security numbers: the history of the Social Security Act and benefits (first payment to Ernest Ackerman, 17 cents, 1937), the 1962 adoption of the SSN as federal ID and taxpayer ID, how the first numbers were issued through employers and post offices with the master file in Maryland, the first number holder John David Sweeney Jr. (001-01-0001 assigned to Grace Owen of Concord, NH, per the hosts), the structure of the nine-digit number (area, group, serial), zip-code-based area numbers, sustainability concerns from the baby boom and Ponzi-scheme debate, who needs an SSN, enumeration at birth, the 1937 wallet with a fake SSN card (Hilda Schrader Whitcher), identity theft and protection advice, getting a new number, and a listener mail correction about dividing and raising to the zero power. Ad read at the start and end.
topics: getting a new Social Security number

segments.title: Opening banter and SSN disclaimer
segments.summary: Hosts open with a sponsor line, banter about accidentally reading out a Social Security number, and tease the topic.

segments.title: Social Security program and Ponzi scheme debate
segments.summary: Explanation that Social Security pays retirees from current workers' taxes, debate over whether it is a Ponzi scheme, and sustainability concerns tied to the baby boom and government treasury bonds.

segments.title: History of Social Security benefits and the SSN
segments.summary: Social Security Act origins, name coined by Abraham Epstein, first payment of 17 cents to Ernest Ackerman in 1937, added benefits in later years, and the 1962 adoption of the SSN as federal ID.

segments.title: How the first numbers were issued
segments.summary: Bureaucratic process: employers reported headcounts on forms, the SSA mailed forms to employers, employees returned them, post offices issued cards, and records were consolidated in Maryland.

segments.title: First Social Security number and the lowest number
segments.summary: John David Sweeney Jr. held the first official number and died before collecting benefits. Grace Owen of Concord, New Hampshire, holds 001-01-0001. Officials declined the number as an honor.

segments.title: How the SSN is structured
segments.summary: Area numbers originally assigned by state from northeast to west, later by zip code; group numbers and serial numbers; discussion of whether the number pool will run out.

segments.title: Who needs an SSN and enumeration at birth
segments.summary: Adults and anyone with income generally need an SSN for banking, tax deductions, medical coverage and government services; Enumeration at Birth lets parents get numbers for newborns.

segments.title: 1937 wallet with fake Social Security card
segments.summary: Douglas Patterson's wallet company included a realistic fake Social Security card with a real number, which was later used by tens of thousands of people.

segments.title: Identity theft and protecting your SSN
segments.summary: Advice on identity theft, avoiding carrying the card, credit card and available-credit ratio, and getting a new number only in extreme cases; warning about companies selling new numbers.

segments.title: Listener mail: dividing and zero exponents
segments.summary: Listener Stephen explains division by zero as containers and why any number to the zero power is not one, following up on an earlier zero episode.
